newsitem.title: UK: British manufacturing shows further signs of recovery.
newsitem.headline: British manufacturing shows further signs of recovery.

text.p: Britain's troubled manufacturing sector continued to recover in September with both output and new orders recording their largest monthly rises since autumn 1994, a key business survey said on Tuesday.

The Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said the Purchasing Managers' Index rose for the fourth successive month, reaching its highest level for 17 months, with the main growth in demand coming from the home market.
But the survey said that while the strongest growth was coming from consumer goods industries, there were the first signs of recovery in the investment goods sector.
"In September, growth appears to have filtered down a further level, to producers of investment goods such as plant machinery," it said.

But while companies have started investing in plant and machinery, there was a reluctance to take on more staff. Roughly the same proportion of companies survey reported a decrease in staff as reported an increase.

Commodity prices fell again but the number of companies reporting a fall in prices dropped to its lowest since January, causing the prices index to move up for its second consecutive month, the survey added.
